html:
The Territory of Papua was southeastern New Guinea under Australian rule. Britain declared a protectorate there in 1884, the same year as German New Guinea in the north, and handed it to Australia in 1906.

For more than thirty years it was run by Lieutenant-Governor Hubert Murray, who protected Papuan land from sale but did little to develop the country. Port Moresby was its capital.

After the Second World War, Australia ran Papua and New Guinea as one territory and prepared them for self-rule. They became independent together as Papua New Guinea in 1975, under Michael Somare. Hiri Motu, the trade language of the Port Moresby coast, is one of the official languages; see Tok Pisin.
